I give up. I could not find a proof I can formalize with confidence, so I have not modified `/work/putnam_2014_a5.lean`.

The mathematical reduction is clear. Write $Q_n(x) = n x^{n+1} - (n+1)x^n + 1 = (x-1)^2 P_n(x)$. Since $P_n(1) = n(n+1)/2 
eq 0$ and $P_n(0) = 1$, a common root $z$ of $P_j$ and $P_k$ must satisfy $z 
eq 0, 1$ and $z^n(nz-(n+1)) = -1$ for $n = j, k$. Showing that this cannot happen for $j 
eq k$ needs a genuinely analytic step (for example, locating the roots of $P_n$ in an annulus, or a modulus argument). I did not find a short argument for that step. Turning it into a Lean proof would also require converting "no common root" into `IsCoprime` in `ℂ[X]`, which adds more work on top of the analysis.
